title: Pregnancy and Birth
hook: For about nine months, a single fertilized cell grows into a baby inside the womb — nourished the whole time by a remarkable temporary organ, the placenta.
key_points: Pregnancy (gestation) is the roughly nine-month period during which a baby develops in the uterus.
The placenta is a temporary organ that passes oxygen and nutrients from parent to fetus and removes wastes.
The umbilical cord connects the fetus to the placenta.
Birth (labor) is the process by which muscular contractions push the baby out of the uterus.
content_html: After fertilization, the new life doesn't simply appear — it grows, sheltered inside the parent's uterus for roughly nine months. This span is called pregnancy, or gestation, and over it a single cell becomes a fully formed baby. Keeping that developing fetus alive requires a dedicated supply line.
extra_html: That supply line is the placenta, a remarkable organ grown specifically for the pregnancy. It draws oxygen and nutrients from the parent's blood and passes them to the fetus, while carrying the fetus's wastes back out — all without the two bloodstreams directly mixing. The fetus is linked to the placenta by the umbilical cord. When development is complete, birth begins: the muscular wall of the uterus contracts in waves during labor, gradually pushing the baby out to take its first breath. NIH MedlinePlus's pregnancy resource describes how the body supports a growing fetus through gestation and into birth.

related.title: Human Reproduction
related.hook: New human life begins when two specialized cells — one egg, one sperm — combine, merging half a set of genetic instructions from each parent into a brand-new whole.

related.title: From Embryo to Baby
related.hook: A single fertilized cell becomes trillions of specialized ones in nine months — dividing, folding, and organizing itself into a heartbeat, a brain, and a body ready to be born.

related.title: Puberty
related.hook: Somewhere around the start of the teenage years, a flood of hormones rewires the body, turning a child into someone capable of one day reproducing.

flashcards.prompt: What is the placenta, and what does it do?
flashcards.back_html: A temporary organ that develops during pregnancy. It passes oxygen and nutrients from parent to fetus and carries away the fetus's wastes, connected by the umbilical cord.

flashcards.prompt: Roughly how long does human pregnancy (gestation) last?
flashcards.explanation_html: Human gestation runs about nine months (around 40 weeks), during which a single fertilized cell develops into a fully formed baby ready to be born.

choices.text: Muscular contractions of the uterus push the baby out
The placenta turns into the baby's first lung
The fetus stops growing and the pregnancy reverses

flashcards.explanation_html: In labor, the muscular wall of the uterus contracts rhythmically, gradually pushing the baby out into the world to begin breathing on its own.
